content:
Weekend plans cancelled? Good. Here are the 5 best shows to stream this weekend — ranked, explained, and sorted by mood so you can stop scrolling and actually watch something.

These picks span Netflix, Max, and beyond. Every one of them is binge-worthy right now.

1. Bridgerton (Netflix)

Genre: Period Drama · Romance | Where to Watch: Netflix | Seasons: 5

Bridgerton is the definition of a binge trap. Set in Regency-era London, the show follows the powerful Bridgerton family as they navigate high society, scandal, and forbidden romance. Think Downton Abbey — but with far more passion and significantly less restraint.

Each season focuses on a different sibling, which means the story stays fresh across five full runs. The production design is extraordinary. The sexual tension is electric. And the twists keep coming.

Why it makes the list: Season 5 is currently streaming, and it's among the show's best work. If you've never started, this weekend is the perfect entry point. If you've already watched — a full rewatch is absolutely worth it.

📺 Stream on: Netflix · Rating: TV-MA · Episodes: 32 · First aired: 2020

2. Wednesday (Netflix)

Genre: Dark Comedy · Mystery · Supernatural | Where to Watch: Netflix | Seasons: 2

Jenna Ortega is Wednesday Addams — and she owns every frame. Enrolled at Nevermore Academy, the deadpan, death-obsessed Wednesday unravels a supernatural mystery while trying (and largely failing) to make friends or care about anyone.

The show balances sharp humour with genuine scares, clever mystery plotting, and surprisingly emotional character beats. Ortega's physical performance is exceptional — the now-iconic dance scene alone made television history.

Why it makes the list: Season 2 deepened everything that made Season 1 great — darker tone, higher stakes, stronger ensemble. If you haven't started, clear your Sunday. If you have, a rewatch before the next season is essential.

📺 Stream on: Netflix · Rating: TV-14 · Episodes: 16 · First aired: 2022

3. Emily in Paris (Netflix)

Genre: Romantic Comedy · Drama | Where to Watch: Netflix | Seasons: 6

Is Emily in Paris perfect television? No. Is it impossibly fun, gorgeous to look at, and impossible to stop watching? Absolutely.

Lily Collins plays Emily Cooper, a plucky American marketing executive who lands in Paris and immediately disrupts everything around her — professionally, romantically, and culturally. The show is pure escapism: beautiful fashion, beautiful city, beautiful mess.

Six seasons in, the show keeps reinventing itself. New cities, new love interests, new professional chaos. The fashion each season is genuinely worth studying — Emily's wardrobe has become as much a talking point as the plot.

Why it makes the list: Perfect for a lazy Sunday when you want comfort TV that also looks stunning. Low-stakes drama, high-quality visuals. For more fashion-forward streaming picks, check our Princess Kate summer style 2026 breakdown.

📺 Stream on: Netflix · Rating: TV-MA · Episodes: 50 · First aired: 2020

4. Outer Banks (Netflix)

Genre: Teen Adventure · Thriller | Where to Watch: Netflix | Seasons: 4+

Outer Banks is exactly what summer weekends were made for. John B and his crew of working-class Pogues go up against the wealthy Kooks in a treasure hunt that gets increasingly dangerous, high-stakes, and completely addictive.

It's part adventure, part class war, part summer romance — and totally over-the-top in the best possible way. The North Carolina coastline setting is gorgeous. The ensemble chemistry is real. And the cliffhangers are ruthless.

Why it makes the list: Once you start, you will not be putting your phone down. The binge pull is elite. Perfect if you want something lighter than Game of Thrones but with the same need to know what happens next energy.

📺 Stream on: Netflix · Rating: TV-MA · Genre: Adventure · First aired: 2020

5. House of the Dragon (Max)

Genre: Fantasy · Epic Drama | Where to Watch: Max (HBO) | Seasons: 3

The Game of Thrones universe is back — and this prequel is arguably better than the original. Set 200 years before Thrones, House of the Dragon chronicles the Targaryen civil war over the Iron Throne. Dragons, political scheming, brutal betrayal, and zero guarantees your favourite character survives the episode.

The production scale is extraordinary. The dragon sequences are the most technically ambitious in television history. And the cast — led by Emma D'Arcy and Matt Smith — delivers performances that rival anything in prestige drama.

Why it makes the list: If you bounced off the later seasons of Game of Thrones, give this one a genuine chance. House of the Dragon has done what few spin-offs manage — it stands entirely on its own.

📺 Stream on: Max (HBO) · Rating: TV-MA · Genre: Fantasy Drama · First aired: 2022

What Should You Watch First This Weekend?

Pick by mood:

  • Craving romance? Bridgerton, Season 1, Episode 1. Go.
  • Want something darker? Wednesday is waiting for you.
  • Need pure escapism? Emily in Paris. No thinking required.
  • Sun and adventure? Outer Banks is peak summer TV.
  • Epic fantasy? House of the Dragon. Clear the whole weekend.

If you're after more picks before hitting play, our Top 10 Romantic Netflix Series list has even more date-night options. And if you're a Stranger Things fan waiting for news, we've got the full Stranger Things Season 5 breakdown covered.
